questions.prompt: You are at a cafe now. Tell me one thing you want to order today — for example an iced coffee, an orange juice, or an egg sandwich. One short sentence, please.
It is evening at home. Tell me one thing you need to do tonight — maybe an email, an exercise video, or an hour of study. Keep it to one short sentence.
questions.context: Talking about tonight's plan at home

questions.prompt: Tell me about one small thing you enjoyed this week — an ice cream, an old movie, an easy walk. Say it in one short sentence.
Your friend asks about your weekend. Tell me one place or thing you'd like to see — an art gallery, an animal cafe, an outdoor market. One short sentence.
After a short team talk at work, tell me one thing you want to make or write first — an action plan, an agenda, an update. One short sentence.
questions.context: Light work talk after a team chat

reason: 명사 앞에 a/an을 빼먹는 습관이 가장 오래 반복되고 있고, 'an'을 'a'처럼 발음하는 문제도 함께 나오니 오늘은 이 둘을 한 문장에서 같이 연습해요.

instruction.sentence_length: one short single-clause sentence, about five to eight words
instruction.hint_timing: wait about five seconds of silence, then give one short hint; correct the 'an' sound right after the learner finishes speaking
contexts: a light work chat with a teammate

level.reason: 짧은 단문은 잘 만들지만 관사와 'an' 발음이 아직 불안정해서 A2에서 더 다듬는 것이 좋아요.

notes: Says 'a meeting' correctly in memorized short patterns, but drops the article when a noun gets longer, like 'project architecture meeting'.
Often breaks one idea into separate fragments ('i had a project meeting.' + 'yesterday.'), so encourage finishing in one breath.
'an' before vowel sounds is pronounced like 'a'; needs the /n/ clearly linked to the next word.
